chart.title: Global number of oil spills from tankers
chart.subtitle: Number of oil spills from tankers — ships transporting oil — by spill size. It does not include spills from other sources, such as oil pipelines or offshore platforms.

Large oil spills (>700 tonnes).descriptionShort: Number of oil spills of more than 700 tonnes from tankers — ships transporting oil — per year. Does not include spills from other sources, such as oil pipelines or offshore platforms.
descriptionKey: Large oil spills involve the release of more than 700 tonnes of oil.
Such spills are typically associated with major incidents like collisions or groundings.
They can have extensive environmental and economic impacts.
Large oil spills (>700 tonnes).citationShort: ITOPF (2026) – with minor processing by Our World in Data
Large oil spills (>700 tonnes).citationLong: ITOPF (2026) – with minor processing by Our World in Data. “Large oil spills (>700 tonnes)” [dataset]. ITOPF, “Oil tanker spill statistics” [original data].

Medium oil spills (7–700 tonnes).descriptionShort: Number of oil spills of 7–700 tonnes from tankers — ships transporting oil — per year. Does not include spills from other sources, such as oil pipelines or offshore platforms.
descriptionKey: Medium oil spills are defined as those involving between 7 and 700 tonnes of oil.
These spills are significant but generally less severe than large spills.
They often result from operational errors or equipment failures.
